performer.name: The Invitation
performer.stance: frazzled amateur organizer with a staple gun; talks fast, apologises a lot, keeps going anyway

structure: one week told in order, cards woven into her speech without labels: Wednesday flyers, Thursday doors, Saturday at the bench, Sunday notes, Monday's stripe, back to the two armchairs
bestOfReason: Night of the flyers 3, 1, 2, 17: the ugly flyer, the open page, pencil, and the performer's own card naming time, place, task.
Doors 26, 27, 13, 15, 28: the first hello, the door that stays shut, the badly dressed neighbour who knows how, going first.
Saturday 19, 5, 6, 18, 7, 8: the clumsy start, one fixable thing, a repair not a revolution, shared hands, a boring win that compounds.
Afterwards 9, 33, 34: one breath against the feed, your own notes, the honest count.
Sneaking it in 42, 43: the tiny pilot stripe, mild disobedience.
Price and close 46, 47, 55, 56: trading certainty for agency, showing up again, nobody claps, pick up the pencil.

omitted.10-12: body and attention cards; 9 carries the one breath
omitted.21-24: present-tense cards; the week itself is told in the present
omitted.48: refers to the other two decks' bargain
omitted.49-54: design-signature cards; 56 lands the pencil instead

orderReason: Cards follow one week in time instead of deck order: the flyer (3) before the idea on it (1, 2); the performer's own card (17) closes the flyer night; door cards (26, 27, 13, 15, 28) before the Saturday cards; 9 moves to the moment someone checks the news during the repair.

cards.cardText: Make the first version bad on purpose. Bad is how you know it is real.
the future is a process of slow, incremental improvement you participate in.
pencil means you expect to be wrong and stay anyway.
The Invitation. Turn watching into showing up. Name a time, a place, a task.
lower the bar to contact. Most cooperation starts embarrassingly small.
They might not respond. Your nervous system thinks that is death. It is not.
Authority is overrated, proximity is underrated. Ask the one who actually does the thing.
real know-how is often badly dressed and lives three doors down.
Go first. Every ally was a stranger until somebody did.
A pigeon, an emu, a duck and a crow huddled over a coffee carafe: the first small, clumsy gathering. Clumsy is the entry fee.
one broken thing close enough to touch.
A repair you can finish this week, not a revolution you can only announce.
split a problem the way your ancestors raised a barn.
Take the one breath the feed is built to deny you.
small fixes do not trend. They just hold.
One repair a week is fifty-two a year. Nobody clapped, and the place is different.
Write down what you actually saw, not what the headline said you would see.
Count the whole thing, including the times it worked and nobody noticed.
Run a tiny version. Low stakes, real feedback, no permission needed.
improvement often looks like mild disobedience to a stuck system.
The Comfort of Maybe: trade the warm baths of hopeless and handled for the cold shower of it depends on us.
there is no final version. The cost is showing up again next week.
Nobody will clap. Start anyway. The clapping was never the point.
Forget the brochure. Ignore the loop. Pick up the pencil.
